sanskrit: saha tārāṅgadābhyāṃ tu saṃgamya hanumān kapiḥ vicinoti sma vindhyasya guhāś ca gahanāni ca
english: Together with Tārā and Aṅgada, Hanūmān the monkey searched through the caves and thickets of the Vindhya.

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlajuṣṭāś ca guhāś ca paritas tathā viṣameṣu nagendrasya mahāprasravaṇeṣu ca
english: They searched all around through caves frequented by lions and tigers, and through the great cascading waterfalls in the rough terrain of that lord of mountains.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tatraiva vasatāṃ sa kālo vyatyavartata
english: As they remained searching there, the allotted time passed away.

sanskrit: sa hi deśo duranveṣo guhā gahanavān mahān tatra vāyusutaḥ sarvaṃ vicinoti sma parvatam
english: That region was hard to explore, vast and filled with caves and dense thickets; yet there Vāyu's son searched every part of the mountain.

sanskrit: paraspareṇa rahitā anyonyasyāvidūrataḥ gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ
english: Separated from one another yet not far from each other, Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, and Gandhamādana searched.

sanskrit: maindaś ca dvividaś caiva hanumāñ jāmbavān api aṅgado yuvarājaś ca tāraś ca vanagocaraḥ
english: Mainda and Dvivida, and likewise Hanūmān and Jāmbavān, and the crown prince Aṅgada, and Tāra who roams the forest.

sanskrit: girijālāvṛtān deśān mārgitvā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam kṣutpipāsā parītāś ca śrāntāś ca salilārthinaḥ avakīrṇaṃ latāvṛkṣair dadṛśus te mahābilam
english: Having searched the southern quarter through regions covered with mountain ranges, overcome by hunger and thirst, exhausted and in need of water, they caught sight of a great cave overgrown with creepers and trees.

sanskrit: tataḥ krauñcāś ca haṃsāś ca sārasāś cāpi niṣkraman jalārdrāś cakravākāś ca raktāṅgāḥ padmareṇubhiḥ
english: Then cranes and geese and sārasas were flying out of it, and wet cakravākas with their limbs reddened by lotus pollen.

sanskrit: tatas tad bilam āsādya sugandhi duratikramam vismayavyagramanaso babhūvur vānararṣabhāḥ
english: Then, having approached that cave which was fragrant and impassable, those bull-like monkeys became minds filled with wonder and eagerness.

sanskrit: saṃjātapariśaṅkās te tad bilaṃ plavagottamāḥ abhyapadyanta saṃhṛṣṭās tejovanto mahābalāḥ
english: Seized by curiosity, those foremost among the leaping monkeys, glowing with energy and possessed of great strength, approached that cave with great excitement.

sanskrit: tataḥ parvatakūṭābho hanumān mārutātmajaḥ abravīd vānarān sarvān kāntāra vanakovidaḥ
english: Then Hanūmān, son of the Wind-god, resembling a mountain peak and skilled in wilderness and forests, addressed all the monkeys.

sanskrit: girijālāvṛtān deśān mārgitvā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam vayaṃ sarve pariśrāntā na ca paśyāmi maithilīm
english: "Having searched the southern quarter through regions covered with mountain ranges, we are all exhausted, and I do not see the Maithilī."

sanskrit: asmāc cāpi bilād dhaṃsāḥ krauñcāś ca saha sārasaiḥ jalārdrāś cakravākāś ca niṣpatanti sma sarvaśaḥ
english: "And from this cave, geese and cranes together with sārasas, and water-wet cakravākas, fly out on all sides."

sanskrit: nūnaṃ salilavān atra kūpo vā yadi vā hradaḥ tathā ceme biladvāre snigdhās tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ
english: "Surely there is water here, whether a well or a pool; and likewise these trees standing at the cave entrance are fresh and lush."

sanskrit: ity uktās tad bilaṃ sarve viviśus timirāvṛtam acandrasūryaṃ harayo dadṛśū romaharṣaṇam
english: Spoken to thus, all the monkeys entered that cave enveloped in darkness, without moon or sun, a sight that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin bile durge nānāpādapasaṃkule anyonyaṃ saṃpariṣvajya jagmur yojanam antaram
english: Then in that cave, difficult to traverse and filled with many kinds of trees, clasping one another mutually, they advanced a distance of a yojana.

sanskrit: te naṣṭasaṃjñās tṛṣitāḥ saṃbhrāntāḥ salilārthinaḥ paripetur bile tasmin kaṃ cit kālam atandritāḥ
english: Losing their senses, thirsty, bewildered, and desperately seeking water, they wandered about within that cave for some time without rest.

sanskrit: te kṛśā dīnavadanāḥ pariśrāntāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ālokaṃ dadṛśur vīrā nirāśā jīvite tadā
english: Those leaping ones, now gaunt, with wretched faces, thoroughly exhausted—those heroes then saw a light ahead, at that point despairing of their lives.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ deśam āgamya saumyaṃ vitimiraṃ vanam dadṛśuḥ kāñcanān vṛkṣān dīptavaiśvānaraprabhān
english: Then, arriving at that place, they saw a pleasant forest free from darkness—golden trees blazing with the radiance of the kindled fire Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit: sālāṃs tālāṃś ca puṃnāgān kakubhān vañjulān dhavān campakān nāgavṛkṣāṃś ca karṇikārāṃś ca puṣpitān
english: Śāla trees, palms, puṃnāgas, kakubhas, vañjulas, dhavas, campankas, nāga trees, and karṇikāras in full bloom.

sanskrit: taruṇādityasaṃkāśān vaidūryamayavedikān nīlavaidūryavarṇāś ca padminīḥ patagāvṛtāḥ
english: Resembling the young sun in color, with altars made of vaidūrya gems, and lotus ponds the hue of blue vaidūrya, thronged with birds.

sanskrit: mahadbhiḥ kāñcanair vṛkṣair vṛtaṃ bālārka saṃnibhaiḥ jātarūpamayair matsyair mahadbhiś ca sakacchapaiḥ
english: Encircled by great golden trees resembling the young sun, and with great fish made of pure gold and tortoises in the waters.

sanskrit: nalinīs tatra dadṛśuḥ prasannasalilāyutāḥ kāñcanāni vimānāni rājatāni tathaiva ca
english: There they saw lotus ponds filled with clear water, and likewise aerial palaces of gold and of silver.

sanskrit: tapanīyagavākṣāṇi muktājālāvṛtāni ca haimarājatabhaumāni vaidūryamaṇimanti ca
english: With windows of refined gold and covered with lattices of pearls, the floors laid with gold and silver and inset with vaidūrya gems.

sanskrit: dadṛśus tatra harayo gṛhamukhyāni sarvaśaḥ puṣpitān phalino vṛkṣān pravālamaṇisaṃnibhān
english: The monkeys saw there on all sides the finest of dwellings, and trees with flowers and fruit, resembling coral and precious gems.

sanskrit: kāñcanabhramarāṃś caiva madhūni ca samantataḥ maṇikāñcanacitrāṇi śayanāny āsanāni ca
english: And golden bees on every side, and honeycombs, and beds and seats marvellous with gems and gold.

sanskrit: mahārhāṇi ca yānāni dadṛśus te samantataḥ haimarājatakāṃsyānāṃ bhājanānāṃ ca saṃcayān
english: They saw on all sides vehicles of great worth, and accumulations of vessels made of gold, silver, and bronze.

sanskrit: agarūṇāṃ ca divyānāṃ candanānāṃ ca saṃcayān śucīny abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: And stores of divine aloe wood and sandalwood, and pure edible roots and fruits.

sanskrit: mahārhāṇi ca pānāni madhūni rasavanti ca divyānām ambarāṇāṃ ca mahārhāṇāṃ ca saṃcayān kambalānāṃ ca citrāṇām ajinānāṃ ca saṃcayān
english: And precious drinks and rich honeys, and stores of divine garments of great worth, and heaps of variegated blankets and of skins.

sanskrit: tatra tatra vicinvanto bile tatra mahāprabhāḥ dadṛśur vānarāḥ śūrāḥ striyaṃ kāṃ cid adūrataḥ
english: Searching here and there in that cave, those radiant and heroic monkeys saw, not far away, a certain woman.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛśasaṃtrastāś cīrakṛṣṇājināmbarām tāpasīṃ niyatāhārāṃ jvalantīm iva tejasā
english: Seeing her, they were greatly startled—a female ascetic clad in bark garment and black antelope skin, of regulated diet, blazing as it were with her own splendor.

sanskrit: tato hanūmān girisaṃnikāśaḥ kṛtāñjalis tām abhivādya vṛddhām papraccha kā tvaṃ bhavanaṃ bilaṃ ca ratnāni cemāni vadasva kasya
english: Then Hanūmān, resembling a mountain, with hands joined in reverence, greeted that venerable woman and asked: "Who are you? Tell us whose is this dwelling, this cave, and these treasures."

sanskrit: ity uktvā hanumāṃs tatra punaḥ kṛṣṇājināmbarām abravīt tāṃ mahābhāgāṃ tāpasīṃ dharmacāriṇīm
english: Having spoken thus, Hanūmān there again addressed that illustrious female ascetic clad in black antelope skin, that one devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: idaṃ praviṣṭāḥ sahasā bilaṃ timirasaṃvṛtam kṣutpipāsā pariśrāntāḥ parikhinnāś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "We have entered suddenly into this cave enveloped in darkness, overcome by hunger and thirst, thoroughly exhausted and distressed in every way."

sanskrit: mahad dhiraṇyā vivaraṃ praviṣṭāḥ sma pipāsitāḥ imāṃs tv evaṃ vidhān bhāvān vividhān adbhutopamān dṛṣṭvā vayaṃ pravyathitāḥ saṃbhrāntāḥ naṣṭacetasaḥ
english: "Thirsty, we entered this great golden cavity; and having seen these various conditions of such astonishing kind, we are disturbed, bewildered, and have lost our wits."

sanskrit: kasyeme kāñcanā vṛkṣās taruṇādityasaṃnibhāḥ śucīny abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: "Whose are these golden trees resembling the young sun, and the pure edible roots and fruits?"

sanskrit: kāñcanāni vimānāni rājatāni gṛhāṇi ca tapanīya gavākṣāṇi maṇijālāvṛtāni ca
english: "Whose are these aerial palaces of gold and the houses of silver, with windows of refined gold and covered with lattices of gems?"

sanskrit: puṣpitāḥ phālavantaś ca puṇyāś surabhigandhinaḥ ime jāmbūnadamayāḥ pādapāḥ kasya tejasā
english: "These trees in flower and fruit, holy and fragrant—these trees made of jāmbūnada gold—by whose power do they exist?"

sanskrit: kāñcanāni ca padmāni jātāni vimale jale kathaṃ matsyāś ca sauvarṇā caranti saha kacchapaiḥ
english: "And golden lotuses grown in the clear water—how is it that golden fish move about together with tortoises?"

sanskrit: ātmānam anubhāvaṃ ca kasya caitat tapobalam ajānatāṃ naḥ sarveṣāṃ sarvam ākhyātum arhasi
english: "The self, the greatness, and the ascetic power—whose is all this? Since all of us do not know, you ought to explain everything to us."

sanskrit: evam uktā hanumatā tāpasī dharmacāriṇī pratyuvāca hanūmantaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratā
english: Addressed thus by Hanūmān, the female ascetic devoted to dharma, delighting in the welfare of all beings, replied to Hanūmān.

sanskrit: mayo nāma mahātejā māyāvī dānavarṣabhaḥ tenedaṃ nirmitaṃ sarvaṃ māyayā kāñcanaṃ vanam
english: "Maya by name—a great-spirited dānava of powerful illusion, the foremost among dānavas—by him all this golden forest was fashioned through māyā."

sanskrit: purā dānavamukhyānāṃ viśvakarmā babhūva ha yenedaṃ kāñcanaṃ divyaṃ nirmitaṃ bhavanottamam
english: "Formerly, he was the Viśvakarman among the foremost of dānavas; by him this divine golden mansion of supreme excellence was fashioned."

sanskrit: sa tu varṣasahasrāṇi tapas taptvā mahāvane pitāmahād varaṃ lebhe sarvam auśasanaṃ dhanam
english: "He performed austerities for thousands of years in the great forest and obtained from the Pitāmaha a boon—all the wealth of Uśanas."

sanskrit: vidhāya sarvaṃ balavān sarvakāmeśvaras tadā uvāsa sukhitaḥ kālaṃ kaṃ cid asmin mahāvane
english: "Having created everything, that powerful one, master of all desires, dwelt happily for some time in this great forest."

sanskrit: tam apsarasi hemāyāṃ saktaṃ dānavapuṃgavam vikramyaivāśaniṃ gṛhya jaghāneśaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
english: "That bull among dānavas, having become attached to the apsarā Hemā, was slain by the lord Purandara, who took up his thunderbolt and struck him by force."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca brahmaṇā dattaṃ hemāyai vanam uttamam śāśvataḥ kāmabhogaś ca gṛhaṃ cedaṃ hiraṇmayam
english: "And this supreme forest was given by Brahmā to Hemā, along with the eternal enjoyment of desires and this golden dwelling."

sanskrit: duhitā merusāvarṇer ahaṃ tasyāḥ svayaṃ prabhā idaṃ rakṣāmi bhavanaṃ hemāyā vānarottama
english: "I am Svayaṃprabhā, the daughter of Merusāvarṇi, her attendant; I guard this dwelling of Hemā, O best of monkeys."

sanskrit: mama priyasakhī hemā nṛttagītaviśāradā tayā dattavarā cāsmi rakṣāmi bhavanottamam
english: "Hemā is my dear friend, skilled in dance and song; given the boon by her, I guard this supreme dwelling."

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ kasya vā hetoḥ kāntārāṇi prapadyatha kathaṃ cedaṃ vanaṃ durgaṃ yuṣmābhir upalakṣitam
english: "What is your purpose, and for what reason do you traverse the wildernesses? And how was this difficult-to-find forest discovered by you?"

sanskrit: imāny abhyavahāryāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca bhuktvā pītvā ca pānīyaṃ sarvaṃ me vaktum arhatha
english: "After eating these edible things, the roots and fruits, and drinking the water, you ought to tell me everything."

sanskrit: atha tān abravīt sarvān viśrāntān hariyūthapān idaṃ vacanam ekāgrā tāpasī dharmacāriṇī
english: Then with single-pointed concentration, the female ascetic devoted to dharma spoke these words to all those troop-leaders among the monkeys who had rested.

sanskrit: vānarā yadi vaḥ khedaḥ pranaṣṭaḥ phalabhakṣaṇāt yadi caitan mayā śrāvyaṃ śrotum icchāmi kathyatām
english: "O monkeys, if your fatigue has passed from eating the fruits, and if this is something I should hear, I wish to hear it—let it be told."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā hanumān mārutātmajaḥ ārjavena yathātattvam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Hearing those words of hers, Hanūmān, son of the Wind-god, began to relate truthfully and straightforwardly exactly what had occurred.

sanskrit: rājā sarvasya lokasya mahendravaruṇopamaḥ rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmān praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam
english: "The glorious Rāma Dāśarathi, king of all the world, comparable to Mahendra and Varuṇa, entered the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā tasya bhāryā janasthānād rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt
english: "Together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife the Vaidehī; his wife was carried off by force from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: vīras tasya sakhā rājñaḥ sugrīvo nāma vānaraḥ rājā vānaramukhyānāṃ yena prasthāpitā vayam
english: "That hero's friend, that king's companion, is a monkey named Sugrīva, king of the foremost monkeys; it is by him that we were dispatched."

sanskrit: agastyacaritām āśāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ yamarakṣitām sahaibhir vānarair mukhyair aṅgadapramukhair vayam
english: "The southern quarter—traversed by Agastya, guarded by Yama—we, together with these foremost monkeys led by Aṅgada."

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ sahitāḥ sarve rākṣasaṃ kāmarūpiṇam sītayā saha vaidehyā mārgadhvam iti coditāḥ
english: "Were charged altogether: 'Search for Rāvaṇa, that rākṣasa who can assume any form at will, together with Sītā the Vaidehī.'"

sanskrit: vicitya tu vayaṃ sarve samagrāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam bubhukṣitāḥ pariśrāntā vṛkṣamūlam upāśritāḥ
english: "Having searched the whole of the southern quarter, all of us, hungry and exhausted, took shelter at the foot of a tree."

sanskrit: vivarṇavadanāḥ sarve sarve dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ nādhigacchāmahe pāraṃ magnāś cintāmahārṇave
english: "All with pallid faces, all absorbed in thought, we could find no end, sunken as we were in the great ocean of worry."

sanskrit: cārayantas tataś cakṣur dṛṣṭavanto mahad bilam latāpādapasaṃchannaṃ timireṇa samāvṛtam
english: "Then casting our eyes about, we saw the great cave, covered over with creepers and trees, enveloped in darkness."

sanskrit: asmād dhaṃsā jalaklinnāḥ pakṣaiḥ salilareṇubhiḥ kurarāḥ sārasāś caiva niṣpatanti patatriṇaḥ sādhv atra praviśāmeti mayā tūktāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "Geese wet with water, their wings beaded with water droplets, ospreys and sārasas flying out from it—I said to the leaping ones, 'Come, let us enter here.'"

sanskrit: teṣām api hi sarveṣām anumānam upāgatam gacchāmaḥ praviśāmeti bhartṛkāryatvarānvitāḥ
english: "And for all of them too the reasoning prevailed: 'Let us go in and enter'—urged on as they were by eagerness for their master's business."

sanskrit: tato gāḍhaṃ nipatitā gṛhya hastau parasparam idaṃ praviṣṭāḥ sahasā bilaṃ timirasaṃvṛtam
english: "Then, having fallen into close formation, grasping one another's hands, we suddenly entered this cave enveloped in darkness."

sanskrit: etan naḥ kāyam etena kṛtyena vayam āgatāḥ tvāṃ caivopagatāḥ sarve paridyūnā bubhukṣitāḥ
english: "This is our situation; it is with this purpose that we came here; and it is to you that all of us have come, exhausted and famished."

sanskrit: ātithyadharmadattāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca asmābhir upabhuktāni bubhukṣāparipīḍitaiḥ
english: "The roots and fruits given by the law of hospitality—these have been consumed by us, who were tormented by hunger."

sanskrit: yat tvayā rakṣitāḥ sarve mriyamāṇā bubhukṣayā brūhi pratyupakārārthaṃ kiṃ te kurvantu vānarāḥ
english: "Since all of us were saved by you when dying of hunger, tell us—for the sake of return service—what the monkeys may do for you."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sarvajñā vānarais taiḥ svayaṃprabhā pratyuvāca tataḥ sarvān idaṃ vānarayūthapam
english: Thus addressed by those monkeys, the all-knowing Svayaṃprabhā then replied to all those leaders of monkey troops.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ parituṣṭāsmi vānarāṇāṃ tarasvinām carantyā mama dharmeṇa na kāryam iha kena cit
english: "I am fully satisfied with all these swift monkeys; while I practise my dharma, there is no service here to be done for me by anyone."
